# Simulated example campaign

**This data is synthetic.** It was generated by
`assaypilot.datasets.simulate_campaign(seed=7)` and describes no real protein,
no real assay, and no real measurement. It exists so that the AssayPilot workflow can be
demonstrated and tested without downloading anything.

Generative model:

- the campaign varies a designed panel of 18 positions, as a real
  engineering effort would; about 10% of candidates also reach
  positions outside that panel, which is what exercises the coverage warnings;
- every (position, residue) pair has a fixed additive effect drawn from N(0, 1);
- 6 pairs of positions interact, with weights drawn from
  N(0, 0.4), so the data is not purely additive;
- each measurement adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.35;
- about 15% of variants were measured twice, so replicate handling is
  exercised;
- measured variants carry 1-6
  substitutions; candidates carry 2-4,
  which makes the candidate pool genuinely harder than the training data.

Files: `measurements.csv`, `candidates.csv`, `campaign.json`, and `ground_truth.csv`
(noise-free values for replay only — the planner never reads it).

## Run it

```bash
assaypilot validate \
  --campaign examples/simulated-enzyme/campaign.json \
  --measurements examples/simulated-enzyme/measurements.csv \
  --candidates examples/simulated-enzyme/candidates.csv

assaypilot plan \
  --campaign examples/simulated-enzyme/campaign.json \
  --measurements examples/simulated-enzyme/measurements.csv \
  --candidates examples/simulated-enzyme/candidates.csv \
  --representation physchem \
  --rank-variability 20 \
  -o example_plan
```

`candidates.csv` uses mutation notation and `measurements.csv` uses full
sequences, so the example exercises both input styles.

`ground_truth.csv` holds the noise-free value behind every sequence. The
planner never reads it; it is there so you can check for yourself how the
selected batch compares with what was achievable.

Regenerate with `python scripts/make_example.py`.
